newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia PM sees good growth, lower interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Latvia PM sees good growth, lower interest rates.

text.p: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele forecast on Friday that gross domestic product (GDP) would grow by three percent in 1996 and interest rates would fall to 15 to 16 percent next year from an average 20 percent currently.
Shkele said the economy this year grew substantially for the first time since 1990, when Latvia began the process of quitting the former Soviet Union.
"GDP has grown to the extent we can now actually feel it for the first time since 1990," Shkele told a news conference.
"I would be satisfied if there turns out to be three percent growth (this year)," he added. "We cannot expect more after the long and difficult year that Latvia has been through."
Latvia last year suffered a serious banking crisis that shrank the economy and swelled the budget deficit to 90 million lats.
Shkele, a non-party businessman, was propelled to power at the start of 1996 specifically to bring some order into government finances and boost the economy.
Shkele said falling interest rates in Latvia were very much a result of a concerted government effort.
He said interest rates are currently an average 20 percent, down from 45 to 50 percent in mid-1995.
"Even 20 percent is too much. We will do all we can to lower interest rates further to an acceptable level, so that they will be within 15 to 16 percent next year," Shkele added.
He said the central bank would continue to lower its key refinancing rate and said he had discussed the issue earlier in the day with central bank president Einars Repshe.
"This means that credit resources available to the national economy will grow," Shkele added.
Shkele sees the passing of a balanced 1997 budget, which he says is vital to cut inflation and encourage growth, as one of his main achievements.
